cues.en: Well, that is a hard act to follow. That was excellent. Thank you. I was actually going to start with something a little serious, which is to say, well, first of all, to say it's been wonderful talking to everybody in the breaks and getting to know you. And one of the things that people say to me often, wherever I go is, boy, I'm so angry that there's this incredible lie. How do I live with this lie about everything that I've been told for so long?
cues.zh: 哎呀，接在这位后面讲可真不容易。刚才讲得太棒了，谢谢。我本来是想先聊点严肃的话题，也就是说，嗯，首先想说的是，茶歇时能和大家交流、认识大家，真的太棒了。而且无论我走到哪里，大家常常跟我说的一句话就是：天哪，我太生气了，居然有这样一个弥天大谎。这么久以来我所被灌输的一切全都是谎言，我该怎么面对？

cues.en: And that is, of course, one of the things that we know. How do you deal with that? Actually, I was going to call my book, The Big Fat Lie. And then we thought, well, that's too aggressive. Let's call it The Big Fat Surprise. And no matter what you call it, surprise, misrepresentation, alt fact. In nutrition science, we've been living this for, in this world, we've all been living this alt fact thing. This is nothing new.
cues.zh: 这当然也是我们熟知的事情之一。你该如何面对它呢？其实，我原本想把我的书命名为《巨大的谎言》（The Big Fat Lie）。后来我们觉得，哎，这太有攻击性了。不如叫《原始的惊奇》（The Big Fat Surprise）吧。但无论你怎么称呼它，惊喜也好、歪曲事实也罢，或是“另类事实”。在营养学界，在这个领域里，我们早就一直生活在这些“另类事实”中了，这根本不是什么新鲜事。

cues.en: I just want to look straight in the camera right now to the YouTube audience and say thank you to the thousands of people who have come out here to hear me speak today. I really appreciate the huge crowd that I see performing. Anyway, okay, let's get down to the science now. So I'm going to talk about vegetable oils.
cues.zh: 我现在想直视镜头，对 YouTube 的观众们说，感谢成千上万今天赶来听我演讲的人，看到现场这么壮观的人群，我真的很感激，不管怎样，好，我们现在开始进入科学部分，今天我要聊聊植物油。

cues.en: What are vegetable oils? These are vegetable oils, the ones that are most commonly known. Really, soybean oil is the one that is really the main contributor to the oil suite. And they're not really vegetable oils. It sounds so lovely, doesn't it? You know, I always wonder about what PR room came up with the word vegetable oil. They're not made from vegetable oils. Vegetables, like broccoli or anything, they're made from seeds and beans.
cues.zh: 什么是植物油？这些就是植物油，也是最常见的一些，实际上，大豆油才是整个油脂家族中的主力，而且它们其实并不是真正的“植物油”，听起来很美好，不是吗？我一直在想，到底是哪个公关团队想出了“植物油”这个词，它们并不是用蔬菜油榨出来的，比如西兰花之类的蔬菜，它们其实是用种子和豆类制成的。

cues.en: There actually should be called seed oils. Amongst technical vegetable oils, vegetable oil scientists, that's actually what they call them among themselves. Of course, they're not natural. These are the natural fats that humans ate for millennia. There's tallow, which comes from cows, and suet from lambs. Lard, these are really the two main ones that were used in cooking in the west. Lard from pigs.
cues.zh: 其实它们应该被称为种子油。在植物油领域的专业科学家之间，他们私下里其实就是这么叫的。当然，它们并不是天然的。这些才是人类食用了数千年的天然脂肪。有来自牛的牛脂，还有来自羊的板油。猪油，这其实是西方烹饪中最主要的两种油脂。猪油来自猪。

cues.en: of course, butter. And in other societies, in Asian societies, they also used coconut oil and palm oil. Those are traditional fats. And we know they're traditional. In the Odyssey, Athena says she lays down a fat goat and the chine of a great wild hog, rich and large, for Odysseus, obviously to kill him. No.
cues.zh: 当然，还有黄油。而在其他社会，比如亚洲社会，人们也会使用椰子油和棕榈油。这些都是传统脂肪。而且我们知道它们历史悠久。《奥德赛》中提到，雅典娜为奥德修斯摆上一只肥山羊和一大块肥美硕大的野猪脊肉，显然是为了害死他？并不是。

cues.en: So vegetable oils, oils of any kind, were really not used for human consumption. They were used for industrial machinery as lubricants in the industrial revolution. I mean, first it was really whale oil from the 1820s to the 1860s, and they were used for machinery. And then when we killed all the whales, we moved over to cottonseed oil, which was a byproduct of, you know, the cotton was a huge crop in the southern United States, and they didn't know what to do with it.
cues.zh: 所以植物油，以及任何种类的油脂，其实都不是供人食用的。它们在工业革命时期是作为工业机械的润滑油使用的。我是说，最开始在1820年代到1860年代主要用的是鲸油，用来润滑机械。后来我们把鲸鱼捕杀殆尽，就转向了棉籽油，这是种植棉花的副产品，你知道，棉花当时是美国南部的一大农作物，人们不知道拿棉籽怎么办。

cues.en: with the leftover oil, so they started using that to replace whale oil. And it wasn't, actually, it was not a food. This oil was used a little bit in the late 1800s to adulterate butter, to kind of sneak it in. But here's the problem with oils and human consumption. They are not stable. They're greasy and oily. So this is just to show you the chemistry. A saturated fatty acid
cues.zh: 不知道怎么处理剩下的油，于是就开始用它来替代鲸油。事实上，它并不是食物。在19世纪末，这种油曾被稍微用于掺假黄油，算是偷偷混进去。但油脂在供人食用时有个问题。它们不稳定，又油腻又黏稠。这里只是给大家展示一下化学结构。饱和脂肪酸

cues.en: has no double bonds in there between the carbon molecules. And so it's straight. A double bond makes a chink in the chain. But if it's saturated, meaning it's saturated with hydrogens, there are no double bonds. So that's straight and flat. And those molecules can sit on top of each other altogether, and there's no space between them. And so they make solids. Saturated fats are solid. Whereas unsaturated fatty acids, this is a polyunsaturated fatty acid. Poly means multiple double bonds.
cues.zh: 其碳分子之间没有双键。因此它是笔直的。双键会在链条中形成一个拐角。但如果是饱和的，意思是氢原子是饱和的，就没有双键。所以它又直又平。这些分子可以完全紧密地叠在一起，彼此之间没有缝隙。所以它们会形成固体。饱和脂肪是固态的。而对于不饱和脂肪酸，这是一种多不饱和脂肪酸。“多”意味着含有多个双键。

cues.en: between the carbons and they're unsaturated because if you broke this bond and put, you could add hydrogens here. So it's not saturated with hydrogens. So, and those molecules don't lie flat together. They're all squiggly and wiggly and so there's space between them and therefore they're oils. That's the basic chemistry. So in order to use oils as food stuff, they had to make them straight.
cues.zh: 在碳原子之间，它们是不饱和的，因为如果打破这个键，就可以在这里加上氢原子。所以它没有被氢原子饱和。这样一来，这些分子就无法紧密平整地贴在一起。它们全都弯弯曲曲的，彼此之间有空隙，因此就成了油。这就是基本的化学原理。所以为了把油用作食材，就必须把它们变直。

cues.en: And they did this through a process called hydrogenation. So they took oleic acid. This is one of the polyunsaturated fats. Actually, that's not polyunsaturated fat. That's the monounsaturated fat. But anyway, the idea is they straighten it out through a process called hydrogenation. And hydrogenation is...
cues.zh: 他们通过一种叫做氢化的工艺做到了这一点。他们使用了油酸。这是多不饱和脂肪的一种。其实不对，那不是多不饱和脂肪，那是单不饱和脂肪。但不管怎么说，关键思路就是通过氢化反应把它变直。而氢化就是……

cues.en: a very complex process that involves all kinds, you know, a huge factor. I actually have been in a hydrogenation factory and, you know, there's just floors and floors of machinery and they use metal catalyst and the hexane solvent and then they go through this incredibly long process because really when you take
cues.zh: 这是一个非常复杂的过程，涉及各种环节，你知道的，厂区非常庞大。我其实去过氢化工厂，你知道，那里一层又一层的全是机器，他们使用金属催化剂和正己烷溶剂，然后经历极其漫长的工序，因为说实话，当你把

cues.en: seeds or beans and you press them, what comes out is this rancid gray liquid and then you have to make that palatable. So you have to deodorize it and winterize it so it's stable and you have to go through all these steps. You don't churn it.
cues.zh: 种子或豆类拿去压榨时，出来的就是这种发臭的灰色液体，然后你得让它变得能入口。所以你必须给它脱臭、冬化脱脂来保持稳定，还得经历所有这些步骤。这可不是搅拌一下就能搞定的。

cues.en: And you don't milk it from a cow and churn it. So it's a lot more complicated. But that process is what allowed vegetable oils to come into the food supply. And that happened because once it could be stabilized, actually, when they first stabilized, this is Proctor and Gamble, who were originally soap makers and tallow makers. And when they first stabilized cottonseed oil in the early 1900s, about 1910 or so, when this process was discovered.
cues.zh: 它不是从牛身上挤出来的奶再拿去搅拌成黄油。所以它要复杂得多。但正是这个工艺让植物油进入了食品供应。之所以能实现，是因为它一旦能被稳定下来——实际上，当他们第一次将其稳定时，正是宝洁（Procter & Gamble）公司，他们最初是做肥皂和动物油脂起家的。1900年代初，大约在1910年左右，这项工艺被发现，他们第一次稳定了棉籽油。

cues.en: They looked at that, and they said, oh, we'll sell that as soap. And actually, a lot of your soaps are made from oils. That's what a lot of soaps are. And then they looked at it, and they said, well, that actually looks a lot like lard. Why don't we try to sell it as lard? And this is in 1911. So they figured that out.
cues.zh: 他们一看，心想，哦，我们可以把它当肥皂卖。其实很多肥皂就是用油脂做的，大部分肥皂都是这样。接着他们又琢磨，这东西其实看着挺像猪油的。要不试着当猪油来卖？那是在1911年，他们就这么琢磨出来了。

cues.en: And they had a number of names where they eventually landed on this idea of Crisco. And that was the introduction of vegetable oils as a commercial product into the human food supply, really. That was really the beginning of it as a commercial product. And they were brilliant about how they went about marketing this product. And they did it, you have to understand, in America, in the early...
cues.zh: 他们想了好多名字，最后选定了 Crisco 这个主意。这其实就是植物油作为商业产品进入人类食物链的开端。这真就是它商业化进程的起点。他们推销这款产品的手法非常高明。你要知道，当时在美国，在20世纪初……

cues.en: particularly in America, almost every society. Everybody wants the new and the modern, and so this was...
cues.zh: 尤其是在美国，乃至几乎所有社会。人人都向往新潮与现代，所以这就像是……

cues.en: They would market Crisco as something, I'm going to quote now, that comes from the book of Crisco. While Crisco may be a shock to the older generation born in an age less progressive than our own, it is a modern woman is glad to give up butter and lard just as her grandmother, quote, her grandmother was happy to forgo the fatiguing spinning wheel. So it was like supposed to be a liberation. It was also marketed in contrast to the
cues.zh: 他们把 Crisco 推销成一种——我现在引用一下《Crisco 之书》里的原话：“虽然对出生在不如当下进步的旧时代的上一辈来说，Crisco 可能会让他们大吃一惊，但现代女性却乐于舍弃黄油和猪油，正如她的祖母”——引用完毕——“当年乐于告别令人疲倦的纺车一样。”所以它本该代表着一种解放。在营销上，它还刻意去对比

cues.en: always sorted conditions of animal slaughter and extraction of animal fats. But Crisco was made in sparkling bright rooms and clean countertops and chemistry labs. And white enamel covers metal surfaces to contrast it to the conditions of making animal fats. And it was incredibly successful.
cues.zh: 屠宰动物和提炼动物油脂时总是污秽不堪的环境。但 Crisco 却是在明亮整洁的房间、一尘不染的台面和化学实验室里生产出来的。金属表面还覆有白色搪瓷，以反衬动物油脂的制作环境。而这种营销策略取得了巨大的成功。

cues.en: They sold cookbooks and all kinds of pamphlets and they marketed it and at the end they said, you know, in every cookbook in America, butter is crossed out and Crisco is put, butter and lard are crossed out and Crisco is put in its place. And that is what happened. At about the same time, margarine also entered. Margarine is also hardened vegetable oils.
cues.zh: 他们售卖食谱和各种宣传小册子，到处做营销，最后他们宣称，全美国的每本食谱上，黄油都被划掉了，取而代之的是 Crisco，黄油和猪油都被划掉，换成了 Crisco。事实也的确如此。差不多在同一时期，人造黄油也粉墨登场了。人造黄油同样是氢化植物油。

cues.en: Originally margarine, very early on, it used to be made with lard and coconut oil, which are solid, stable fats. But by 1958, it was made entirely from polyunsaturated fats. And it was a huge threat to the dairy industry. If you want any insight into why one of the reasons it took me so long to write a book is that, you know, I spent like three months completely obsessed with margarine and went into it. There was this whole incredible chapter of the dairy industry trying to...
cues.zh: 最初的人造黄油，在非常早期的时候，是用猪油和椰子油制成的，这些都是固态且稳定的脂肪。但到了 1958 年，它已经完全由多不饱和脂肪制成了。这对乳制品行业构成了巨大的威胁。如果你想知道我写这本书为什么花了这么长时间，其中一个原因就是，我大概有整整三个月完全沉迷于人造黄油，深入探究了进去。乳制品行业曾有过一段令人难以置信的抗争历史，试图……

cues.en: to prevent the margarine industry from entering in and so they had all kinds of taxes and restrictions and you couldn't sell yellow margarine you had to only sell it as white and then you would get a little color capsule that you would need into it to make it yellow to look like butter and these are angry housewives protesting that they want their margarine because of course vegetable oils were very quickly cheaper.
cues.zh: 为了阻止人造黄油行业的进入，他们出台了各种税收和限制，甚至不能卖黄色的人造黄油，只能卖白色的，买的时候会附赠一个小色素胶囊，得自己揉进去把它染成黄色，看着像真黄油一样；而这些愤怒的家庭主妇正在抗议，要求买到人造黄油，因为植物油很快就便宜得多了。

cues.en: They were just cheaper, so Housewives wanted them. And eventually it became accepted really in World War II when even wealthy women wanted to save money and it was considered okay then to put margarine on an elegant table. And so that was sort of the end of margarine restrictions.
cues.zh: 它们就是便宜，所以主妇们都想要。最终直到二战时期它才真正被广泛接受，当时就连富家太太也想省钱，在讲究的餐桌上摆人造黄油也变得无可厚非了。人造黄油的种种限制，差不多也就这样走向了终结。

cues.en: So Crisco and margarine are the main ways that vegetable oils entered into our food supply. And that all happened. Really, they were introduced solidly in the food supply by the mid-20th century. And then when did oil as oil come in? This actually happened in the 1940s because by 1940, they had figured out how to stabilize oil.
cues.zh: Crisco 起酥油和人造黄油是植物油进入我们饮食的主要途径。这一切都发生了。事实上，到了 20 世纪中叶，它们就已经牢牢占据了食品供应的一席之地。那么，纯粹作为液态油的食用油又是何时登场的呢？这其实发生在 20 世纪 40 年代，因为直到 1940 年，他们才摸索出稳定油质的方法。

cues.en: just enough to sell it in a bottle. Remember, oils are rancid products. They oxidize really easily. They go rancid and bad. They have no shelf life stability, but they figured out a little chemical fix in the 1940s, and so now they were able to sell it as oils. And then, of course, as we know, they got a huge boost when the American Heart Association started recommending polyunsaturated
cues.zh: 刚好够装在瓶子里卖。别忘了，油是容易酸败的产物。它们极易氧化，会酸败变质，毫无保质期稳定性可言，但他们在 20 世纪 40 年代找到了一个化学小妙招，于是现在能把它当成液态油来卖了。接着，正如我们所知，当美国心脏协会开始推荐多不饱和

cues.en: vegetable oils to replace saturated fats. And this was a tremendous boost to the vegetable oil industry. As we know, that was all part of Ansel Keys' diet-heart hypothesis. We said saturated fats and cholesterol cause heart disease. And that happened in response to the tremendous panic over the rising tide of heart disease, with President Eisenhower himself having a heart attack in 1955 and being out of the Oval Office for 10 whole days. Just imagine your president is out of the office.
cues.zh: 植物油来替代饱和脂肪时，它们迎来了巨大的推力。这对植物油产业来说是一剂强心针。众所周知，这全都是 Ancel Keys 的“饮食-心脏假说”的一部分。我们曾认为饱和脂肪和胆固醇会导致心脏病。而这一切的发生，是对心脏病激增所引发的巨大恐慌的回应，就连 Eisenhower 总统本人也在 1955 年突发心脏病，整整 10 天无法在椭圆形办公室办公。想象一下，你们的总统连续多日无法处理政务。

cues.en: you know, for 10 days. I mean, like, really, I mean, the nation was in a tremendous panic. And it was into that vacuum of understanding about what causes heart disease that Ansel Keyes stepped. And this is just my chart to show you what an incredibly ludicrous idea it was at the time that President Eisenhower's heart attack was caused by saturated fats already declining in the food supply. What was...
cues.zh: 你知道，持续了整整10天。我是说，真的，举国上下陷入了极大的恐慌。正是在对心脏病成因认知的这一空白期，Ansel Keyes 站了出来。这只是我做的一张图表，用来向大家展示在当时看来多么荒谬的想法：艾森豪威尔总统的心脏病，竟然被归咎于在食品供应中已经在减少的饱和脂肪。而真正……

cues.en: Perfectly rising in lockstep with heart disease was unsaturated vegetable oils. So how crazy to think that you would solve a condition with the food that had been just invented and seemed to be perfectly correlated with heart disease.
cues.zh: 与心脏病发病率完全同步攀升的，是不饱和植物油。所以，想用一种刚被发明出来、而且似乎与心脏病完全正相关的食物来解决这个问题，这想法有多疯狂。

cues.en: Anyway, and there's also a really interesting back story about how the American Heart Association had really had deep, deep ties with the vegetable oil industry and in fact had been launched by Procter & Gamble, a vegetable oil, one of their products was Crisco.
cues.zh: 不管怎么说，这里面还有一个非常耐人寻味的幕后故事：美国心脏协会（American Heart Association）实际上与植物油行业有着极深极深的利益瓜葛，它其实就是由宝洁公司（Procter & Gamble）发起的，而宝洁旗下的植物油产品之一就是 Crisco。

cues.en: Procter & Gamble, the original maker of Crisco. And this is a story that I tell in my book that, the American Heart Association, understand because heart disease really only came, was rare until the late 1920s, the American Heart Association, cardiologist was a relatively small little specialty, and they were, they were,
cues.zh: 宝洁公司是 Crisco 最初的制造商。我在书里讲过这个故事，美国心脏协会——要知道，心脏病在 20 世纪 20 年代末之前其实很罕见，所以美国心脏协会、心脏病学在当时只是个相对小众的领域，他们当时……他们当时……

cues.en: They were not a big group and they had an office, a small office and almost no money. The American Heart Association really was nothing to look at until the Proctor and Gamble came along in 1948 and they designated them to be the recipient of this Jack Benny radio show contest. It's called The Walking Men Contest where all the proceeds from the show went to the American Heart Association. And as the American Heart Association's own history book reads, it says, and overnight,
cues.zh: 他们并不是个大组织，只有一间小办公室，而且几乎没什么钱。在 1948 年宝洁公司找上门之前，美国心脏协会根本无足轻重。宝洁指定他们作为 Jack Benny 广播电台竞赛的受益方。那个比赛叫“徒步者竞赛”，节目的所有收益都捐给了美国心脏协会。正如美国心脏协会自己的历史书中所写：一夜之间，

cues.en: millions flew into our, poured into our coffers. As the Procter & Gamble man, they had a dinner celebrated and handed us the check, and overnight they became a huge, massive nonprofit organization. They're still the biggest nonprofit in the US today, all thanks to their launch by Procter & Gamble, whom they paid off, I think, very well. And because they were recommending
cues.zh: 数百万美元涌入了我们的金库。宝洁公司的人举办了一场晚宴庆祝，并把支票交给了我们，他们一夜之间就变成了一个庞大的非营利组织。他们至今仍是美国最大的非营利机构，这全拜宝洁公司的提携所赐，而我认为他们也给了宝洁丰厚的回报。因为他们当时在推荐……

cues.en: Crisco products. In fact, there's a story that I don't have the picture of it, but there's a story of a, I have a letter from a scientist complaining to Campbell Moses, who is the president of the American Heart Association in the 1960s saying, you know, Campbell, I can't believe the rank commercialism of your posing in that film with your face next to a bottle of Crisco oil.
cues.zh: Crisco 的产品。事实上还有这么个故事，我虽然没找到照片，但我有一封信，是一位科学家写给 20 世纪 60 年代美国心脏协会主席 Campbell Moses 的投诉信，信中说：Campbell，我真不敢相信你在那部影片里，居然把脸贴在一瓶 Crisco 油旁边摆拍，简直太商业化了。

cues.en: And I won't participate if you continue to do that. So the American Heart Association, so what this enabled the vegetable oil industry to do was to market itself basically as a health food, as a food that you can eat in order to avoid a heart attack.
cues.zh: 如果你继续那样做，我就不参与了。所以美国心脏协会——这让植物油行业得以把自己基本上包装成一种健康食品，一种吃了能避免心脏病的食品。

cues.en: These are some more ads. Take this ad to your doctor so they can prescribe vegetable oils to you. And here's margarine for because of course your eight-year-old should worry about cholesterol. That actually, that ad actually became the subject of a whole lawsuit and was eventually banned because there was no evidence and still is no evidence that high cholesterol in children has anything to do with heart disease except for in rare genetic cases.
cues.zh: 这还有一些广告。“拿着这个广告去找你的医生，让他们给你开植物油。” 还有这个讲人造黄油的，因为“你八岁的孩子当然也该担心胆固醇”。实际上，那个广告引发了一场官司，并最终被禁，因为根本没有任何证据——到现在也没有证据——表明儿童高胆固醇与心脏病有关，极少数遗传病例除外。

cues.en: Let's see testing the diet heart hypothesis. This is just to let you know that That this whole idea that saturated fats replacing saturated fats with polyunsaturated fats has been tested in large randomized controlled clinical trials on
cues.zh: 来看看针对“饮食-心脏假说”的检验。这只是为了告诉大家，用多不饱和脂肪替代饱和脂肪的这套理论，已经在大型随机对照临床试验中接受过检验，

cues.en: more people than have ever been tested on any other hypothesis in the world, in nutrition science, and the results, you know, large, well-controlled tiles, which are the gold standard of evidence, and they have shown no effect of saturated fat on any cardiovascular mortality or total mortality. So, that and that...
cues.zh: 参与测试的人数比营养科学界针对任何其他假说测试的人都要多，而结果——要知道，大型、严格受控的试验可是证据的金标准——结果显示，饱和脂肪对任何心血管死亡率或总死亡率都没有影响。所以，这一点……

cues.en: that knowledge is part of the alt-fat world that we live in, which is that nobody talks about that. So one of the reasons I wanted to bring up those studies is that in those trials, in all those trials, they tended to replace regular fats with lard and meat, and then they would replace those with vegetable oils, right?
cues.zh: 这种认知属于我们所处的“另类脂肪”世界的一部分，那就是根本没人谈论这个。所以我之所以想提到那些研究，是因为在所有的那些试验中，他们往往是用猪油和肉类替代常规脂肪，然后再用植物油来替换它们，对吧？

cues.en: In effect, you're studying a number of things in those trials, but one of the things you're studying is, well, what is the effect of having a high vegetable oil diet? If you have a lot of corn oil and soybean oil, what happens? Well, in nearly a dozen of these studies, they found a number of worrisome things, including that in all the experimental groups, they died at higher rates of cancer. So this is the LA Veterans Study.
cues.zh: 实际上，你在那些试验中研究了很多东西，但其中一项是：高植物油饮食究竟有什么影响？如果你摄入大量的玉米油和大豆油，会发生什么？在近十几项此类研究中，他们发现了一些令人担忧的现象，包括所有实验组的癌症死亡率都更高。这就是洛杉矶退伍军人研究。

cues.en: where the men ate diets high in soy, corn, safflower, cottonseed oil. Six years of this wasn't a perfect trial. They didn't control for smoking, say. But it was successful. I mean, one of the markers of a successful trial is that the men did successfully lower their cholesterol, as they did in all the diet heart trials. But they died at more than twice the rate of the control group from cancer.
cues.zh: 受试男性食用了大量大豆油、玉米油、红花油和棉籽油。这长达六年的试验并不完美，比如他们没有控制吸烟变量。但它成功了。我是说，成功试验的标志之一，就是这些男性的胆固醇确实成功降了下来，就像所有饮食心脏试验一样。但他们死于癌症的几率是对照组的两倍多。

cues.en: And that was found in another, in another, at other trials as well. They also had two times higher rates of gallstones. Gallstones was found in another cholesterol-lowering trial. So maybe it's the vegetable oils, maybe it's the cholesterol lowering, we don't know. Strokes, also found in people who have lower, at much higher rates, in people who have lower cholesterol. And in fact, the pure,
cues.zh: 在其他试验中也有同样的发现。他们患胆结石的概率也高出两倍。在另一项降胆固醇试验中也发现了胆结石。所以可能是植物油的原因，也可能是胆固醇降低本身引起的，我们不得而知。胆固醇较低的人群中，中风的发生率也高得多。事实上，PURE——

cues.en: Study that just came out recently, which was the largest ever epidemiological study ever undertaken, they found that the lower the saturated fat, the people who ate the lowest amount of saturated fat had the highest risk of stroke. So whether or not that's the low amount of saturated fats or the high amount of vegetable oils they're eating or the low cholesterol, we don't know. But that's a disturbing finding that is clearly now echoing through this work.
cues.zh: 最近刚公布的这项有史以来规模最大的流行病学研究发现，饱和脂肪摄入量越低，也就是那些摄入饱和脂肪最少的人，中风的风险反而最高。因此，无论是因为饱和脂肪摄入过低、食用植物油过多，还是胆固醇偏低，我们都无法确定。但这确实是一个令人不安的发现，显然正在这项研究中不断得到印证。

cues.en: Also possible cirrhosis of the liver that was found in more than just that study there. So worrisome side effects of switching your diet over to vegetable oils from saturated fats and was in fact so worrisome that the NIH had a series of high level meanings on this at which people like Ansel Keys and his buddies were all invited to try to figure out what was going on with these trials, why the higher rates of cancer and gallstones.
cues.zh: 而且不止那项研究发现了可能导致的肝硬化。因此，把饱和脂肪换成植物油的饮食转变带来了令人担忧的副作用，事实上这令人担忧到 NIH 为此举行了一系列高规格会议，邀请了像 Ansel Keys 和他的同行们，试图弄清楚这些试验到底是怎么回事，为什么癌症和胆结石的发生率会更高。

cues.en: And they had, so this is three separate years they had these meetings, and they had various ideas. They thought that maybe low cholesterol was a sign of getting cancer. Anyway, in the end, they just decided that lowering cholesterol was too important. Heart disease was, it was too important to fight heart disease, and they didn't want any kind of other message getting in the way of their cholesterol lowering advice.
cues.zh: 他们举行了，这些会议一共分三年举行，他们提出了各种想法。他们认为胆固醇偏低可能是患癌的征兆。不过不管怎样，他们最终还是认定降低胆固醇更为重要。心脏病是……抗击心脏病太重要了，他们不想让任何其他信息干扰到他们关于降低胆固醇的建议。

cues.en: But this just shows you the rise in vegetable oils over the course. It's actually, it is the food group that has more than any other food group, it has risen the most. So it's like our consumption of it has gone from zero to seven to eight percent of all calories that we consume in the U.S., which is just like 121,000 times more than we ate in 1900. And now it's mostly soybean oil.
cues.zh: 但这正好向你展示了植物油在这段时期的激增。事实上，它比任何其他类别的食物增长都要迅猛。我们在美国的植物油摄入量，从几乎为零一路飙升至占总热量的7%到8%，比1900年的摄入量翻了差不多12.1万倍。而现在它主要就是大豆油。

cues.en: So why, why do we have this astronomic rise? Well, obviously there's the fact that the American Heart Association is supporting this idea, then the US Dietary Guidelines get on board and they say replace
cues.zh: 那为什么，为什么会出现这种天文数字般的暴涨呢？显然，事实是美国心脏协会支持这种观点，随后《美国膳食指南》也加入进来，建议大家用

cues.en: your saturated fats with polyunsaturated vegetable oils, although it doesn't say that quite there, but it does. And then there's that hydrogenated oil becomes the backbone of the food industry. So, you know, almost every food in these supermarket aisles is comprised of, you know, usually it's mainly like some sugar, grain, and then they need a fat. You need a fat to make any cookie cracker crisp, anything. And that fat
cues.zh: 多元不饱和植物油替代饱和脂肪，虽然字面上没那么直白，但意思就是这样。接着，氢化油成了食品工业的支柱。你知道，超市货架上的几乎每种食物，通常主要都是糖类、谷物，然后还需要油脂。要做出饼干、脆饼、脆片等任何零食，都少不了油脂。而这种油脂

cues.en: is hydrogenated soybean oil. That's just always the way it was. And because it's cheap, it's easy to manipulate. And so every one of these products contains hydrogenated oils, or did until quite recently. These are the natural alternatives. These are the non-animal based natural alternatives that can also be used by...
cues.zh: 就是氢化大豆油。向来都是这样。因为成本低，容易加工。所以直到最近，每款这类产品都含有氢化油。这些就是天然替代品，这些非动物源的天然替代品，还可以用于……

cues.en: food manufacturers and indeed were. And for a good part, up until the 80s, these were used by food companies in their products. And they're healthier because they're more stable and because they're naturally solid. They don't have to go through that hydrogenation process to become solid.
cues.zh: 食品制造商确实使用过。在80年代之前的很长一段时间里，食品公司都在产品中使用这类油脂。而且它们更健康，因为性质更稳定，并且天生就是固态的。它们不需要经过氢化过程来变成固体。

cues.en: But these were sort of scared out of the US food supply because for a number of reasons that are really fascinating. One was the American Soybean Association recognized that the tropical oils were a threat to them. And so they came up with this idea. This is Steve Drake, who is the head of the American Soybean Association when they were doing this whole campaign from 1986 to 1989.
cues.zh: 但出于一些非常耐人寻味的原因，这些油脂在某种程度上被恐吓退出了美国食品供应链。原因之一是，美国大豆协会（American Soybean Association）意识到热带油脂对他们构成了威胁。于是他们想出了这个主意。这位是 Steve Drake，他在1986年到1989年发起这场全方位宣传战时，正担任美国大豆协会的会长。

cues.en: And they distributed all these fat fighter kits. What you don't know about tropical oils will kill you. And they pictured sleazy Asians with cigars saying, putting the wholesome American farmer out of business. And then they came up with the term tree lard, which sounds really appealing and definitely had an effect. And I just put this up because I see echoes of this.
cues.zh: 他们分发了所有这些“脂肪斗士”宣传包，上面写着：“关于热带油脂，你不知道的事会要了你的命。”他们还画了抽着雪茄、面相猥琐的亚洲人，宣称这让健康的美国农民濒临破产。接着他们又造出了“树上长出的猪油”这个词，听起来极具吸引力，也确实收到了成效。我把它展示出来，只是因为我在其中看到了历史的影子。

cues.en: Really, a couple people have mentioned that this recent American Heart Association presidential advisory, they focus quite a lot on coconut oil. They're like, why are they focusing on coconut oil? This is in their heart news, which I just have to say is an aside. Here they're creating the controversy, and then here they're saying, why all the hubbub? Over the controversy we're creating. That's just such a classic tactic.
cues.zh: 确实，好几个人都提到，美国心脏协会最近发布的这份主席咨询报告，把焦点放在了椰子油上。大家都在纳闷：他们为什么总揪着椰子油不放？这是他们发布的心脏健康新闻，顺便说一句，他们在这边挑起争议，转过头又在那边问：大家为什么吵得这么凶？明明这争议就是他们自己制造的。这手段简直太经典了。

cues.en: They do, they really emphasize coconut oil. Coconut oil does not have any different kind of saturated fats than any of the other saturated fats that have all been tested in those randomized controlled clinical trials, finding no effect on mortality. So why are they focusing on coconut oil? Well, you know, it may be that they receive lots of money. This is just one of the things that I happened to found because it actually was somebody who was stupid enough to put this on the web. But, you know,
cues.zh: 他们确实在大力强调椰子油。但椰子油里的饱和脂肪，跟其他所有做过随机对照临床试验的饱和脂肪没有任何不同，那些试验都证明它对死亡率没有影响。那他们为什么非要盯着椰子油呢？这个嘛，可能是因为他们拿了不少钱。这只是我碰巧发现的事情之一，因为居然真有人蠢到把它发在网上。但是，你们懂的，

cues.en: They get a lot of money from soybean companies, vegetable oil companies, and so maybe that's the reason. Maybe coconut oil is still a threat to them. Coconut oil has certainly experienced a real resurgence, tropical oils have experienced a resurgence in the US.
cues.zh: 他们从大豆公司、植物油公司拿了大量资金，这也许就是原因吧。可能椰子油对他们来说依然是个威胁。在现在的美国，椰子油确实迎来了真正的复兴，热带油脂整体上都在卷土重来。

cues.en: Back in the 80s, another reason that we saw a rise in polyunsaturated hydrogenated oils is that there was this passionate Nebraska millionaire, Philip Sokoloff, who took out all these ads. He really believed that tropical oils were killing people. He was one of those passionate, uninformed people.
cues.zh: 回到80年代，多不饱和氢化油兴起的另一个原因，是内布拉斯加州有一位叫 Philip Sokoloff 的狂热百万富翁，他刊登了大量广告。他坚信热带油脂正在害死人们。他就是那种狂热却又无知的人。

cues.en: And we are not going to name any names right now. But we all know them. And he went on this. He just spent all his money. He had suffered a heart attack, thought that going on a prudent plant-based diet was what saved him. And now he was going to save the rest of America. And he took out all these ads. And he had everybody call every executive at all the major food companies. And that had an extraordinary effect of all of our big food companies, Nabisco, Kraft.
cues.zh: 我们现在就不指名道姓了。但大家都知道这种人。他对此非常投入。他花光了自己所有的积蓄。他曾突发过心脏病，认为是转向谨慎的植物性饮食救了他。现在他要去拯救全美国的人。他刊登了所有这些广告。他还号召大家给各大食品公司的高管打电话。这给 Nabisco、Kraft 等所有大型食品公司带来了巨大的影响。

cues.en: everybody just getting at pulling out all their palm oil and coconut oil and switching over to hydrogenated polyunsaturated oils.
cues.zh: 大家都在把棕榈油和椰子油统统换掉，改用氢化多不饱和油。

cues.en: So, and then there's also our friends, CSPI, for those of you who saw my talk yesterday, they're the ones who were in charge of the retraction letter, always on the right side of science, and they were saying, they've always been against saturated fats, and they were pushing trans fats, and they did this particularly in movie theaters, getting rid of any kind of butter popcorn, or coconut oil popcorn, and they got rid of all the fats in restaurants, and all the fryers.
cues.zh: 然后还有我们的老朋友 CSPI，听过我昨天演讲的人都知道，撤稿信就是他们带头搞的，他们总是自诩站在科学正确的一方，他们一直反对饱和脂肪，大力推崇反式脂肪，在电影院尤其卖力，取缔了黄油爆米花和椰子油爆米花，还清除了餐馆和油炸锅里的所有这类油脂。

cues.en: So this meant that there was, by the end of the 1980s, all the fats used in restaurants and processing and food service and cafeterias everywhere was hydrogenated vegetable oils. And I'm sure it's a similar situation for in this country and others. But then, whoops.
cues.zh: 这意味着到20世纪80年代末，餐馆、食品加工、餐饮业和各个食堂所用的油脂，全变成了氢化植物油。我相信在这个国家和其他地方情况也差不多。但是接着，哎呀，搞砸了。

cues.en: Partially hydrogenated vegetable oils contain trans fats, and these are some of the original researchers who were interested and involved in figuring out understanding trans fats and understanding their role and why they were potentially a danger to health.
cues.zh: 部分氢化植物油含有反式脂肪，而这些就是最早对此感兴趣并参与其中的研究人员，他们致力于搞清反式脂肪的机理、作用，以及为什么它可能危害健康。

cues.en: Not due to their work, but eventually when Harvard caught whiff of it and Harvard decided to get involved then the FDA decided to ban trans fats and I don't know what the situation is with trans fats here, but It's not bad. It's not banned so Well, I'll just tell you a little story about it trans fats were banned because they slightly raise LDL cholesterol So we all know what we think of LDL cholesterol
cues.zh: 反式脂肪被禁并非归功于他们的工作，而是当哈佛大学最终察觉并决定介入后，FDA才决定禁用它。我不知道这里对反式脂肪的政策是怎样的，但还没有完全禁用，所以……好吧，我来给大家讲个关于它的小故事：反式脂肪被禁，是因为它会轻微升高LDL胆固醇，我们大家都清楚自己是怎么看待LDL胆固醇的。

cues.en: And I don't think that was a correct reason for banning them. They were also banned largely on the basis of epidemiological data. However, trans fats, those other researchers I just showed you, they did find a number of other disturbing health effects of trans fats, which makes me not sorry they're banned, even if it was for the wrong reasons. But the problem is, what replaces trans fats? This is a huge issue. And again,
cues.zh: 我认为这不是禁用它的合理解释。它们很大程度上也是基于流行病学数据被禁的。不过，我刚才给你们看的那批研究人员，确实发现了反式脂肪其他一些令人担忧的健康影响，这让我觉得即便禁用的理由不对，被禁了也没什么好可惜的。但问题是，拿什么来替代反式脂肪呢？这是一个巨大的难题。而且，

cues.en: You have to remember, this is the polyunsaturated molecule not stable. It's not stable unless it's hydrogenated. So still not stable. If you can't hydrogenate it, it's not a stable molecule. And so vegetable oil companies started going back to all their chemistry labs and figuring out, well, what were they going to use? They needed a new, newfangled something or other to replace hydrogenated fats. And this is what they've come up with. So they've genetically modified soybeans.
cues.zh: 大家必须记住，多不饱和分子是不稳定的。除非经过氢化，否则它就不稳定。所以它依然不稳定。如果不能氢化，它就不是一个稳定的分子。于是，植物油公司开始重新钻进化学实验室，琢磨到底该用什么。他们需要某种新奇的替代品来取代氢化脂肪。这就是他们拿出的成果：他们对大豆进行了基因改造。

cues.en: to produce less of the particular fatty acids that seem to cause rancidity, like linoleic, linolenic. They've tried to change the expression of those particular fatty acids. A lot more sunflower oil, which is naturally a little more stable, has come out because it's higher in some monounsaturated fats. And then they've made this thing called intra-sterified oils.
cues.zh: 减少生成那些容易导致酸败的特定脂肪酸，比如亚油酸、亚麻酸。他们试图改变这些特定脂肪酸的表达。市面上出现了更多的葵花籽油，因为它天然含有更高的单不饱和脂肪，相对更稳定一些。接着他们又制造出了这种所谓的“酯交换油”。

cues.en: where they take each triglyceride in a fatty acid, they have triglycerides, they swap around the actual carbon molecules. Anyway, that is, who knows what that is? And probably another trans fats in 20 years time. And all of these are expensive options. What we really should do is just go back to using saturated fats, right? We should just go back to using
cues.zh: 他们取出脂肪酸中的每个甘油三酯——油脂里含有甘油三酯——然后重新调换其中的碳分子结构。不管怎样，谁知道那到底是什么东西？搞不好过个20年，它又成了另一种反式脂肪。而且这些全都是昂贵的技术手段。我们真正该做的，其实就是重新用回饱和脂肪，对吧？我们本该直接用回

cues.en: lard and tallow and suet, natural, non-oxidizing, but we can't because our dietary guidelines put a limit on saturated fat. So that's why we have in all of our restaurants still, you know, they're just using the cheapest option. So this is what I wanted to say, which is the other way in which we talk about...
cues.zh: 猪油、牛油和板油，这些天然且不易氧化的油脂，但我们不能，因为膳食指南限制了饱和脂肪的摄入。这就是为什么我们所有的餐馆里，如你所知，依然只选用成本最低的那种油。所以这就是我想说的，关于我们探讨此事的另一个维度……

cues.en: the polyunsaturated fats is that these are omega-6s. That's another way you might have heard of them. And they are, omega-6s are known to have inflammatory effects, right? And part of the reason for just showing you this chart is that we get...
cues.zh: 这些多不饱和脂肪其实就是 omega-6 脂肪酸，你可能听说过这种叫法。大家都知道 omega-6 会引发炎症反应，对吧？我展示这张图表的部分原因，就是想说明我们摄入的……

cues.en: You get some omega-6s in nuts and in other places. Most of them come from vegetable oils. And probably some of you, you've heard of the omega-3 omega-6 ratio. You're supposed to keep that ratio relatively high in omega-3s and relatively low in omega-6s. And people are always telling you, spend a lot of money on omega-3s to get that ratio up. Well, you're never going to have, or maybe some of you do. But if you're eating a lot of vegetable oils,
cues.zh: 坚果和其他食物里也有一些 omega-6，但大部分都来自植物油。你们中有些人可能听说过 omega-3 和 omega-6 的比例，理想状态是 omega-3 相对高一些，omega-6 相对低一些。大家总会劝你花大价钱买 omega-3 来提高这个比例。然而你根本达不到，或者可能少数人能做到。但如果你吃了大量的植物油，

cues.en: You're going to be spending a fortune in your omega 3s to get your omega 3s ratio up. The best way to get that ratio, if you believe in it, in good shape is to just not have omega 6s. Keep your omega 6s down. And even healthy people who tend to binge on nuts might be having too many omega 6s. So you do have to wash out for that, especially with all these new nut flowers around that people are baking with. So it's just something to be aware of.
cues.zh: 你得花巨资买 omega-3 才能把比例拉上去。要想把这个比例维持在理想状态——如果你相信这套理论的话——最好的办法就是少吃 omega-6，把 omega-6 的摄入量降下来。即使是那些习惯狂吃坚果的健康人群，摄入的 omega-6 也可能会超标。所以大家确实得小心这一点，尤其是现在市面上冒出了各种大家用来烘焙的坚果粉。总之留个心眼就好。

cues.en: This is to show you what is happening in restaurant fryers across the...
cues.zh: 这是为了向大家展示，在全美餐馆油炸锅里……

cues.en: across the country is that they are using, they've just gone back to regular soybean oil, corn oil, and this is another thing, I bring this up also for this crowd who probably is very health conscious, but you may not know what your oil, the restaurant that you go to is frying in. And I know in America, all the McDonald's, all the, every fast food chain, and really it's not even the fast food chains that, which probably you avoid, but every,
cues.zh: 全美各地正在发生的事情是，他们重新用起了普通大豆油、玉米油，还有一点，我对在座各位提这个，是因为大家可能非常注重健康，但你可能并不清楚自己常去的餐馆用什么油来炸食物。而且我知道在美国，所有的 McDonald's、所有的快餐连锁店——其实不仅是你们可能避而远之的快餐连锁店，而且是每一家……

cues.en: every mom and pop restaurant where they have fried food, they're frying in just regular oils. And I don't think I have time to go into the whole story of how scary heated vegetable oils are. And I'm not, you know, flogging my book, but I will tell you at the end of Chapter 9, should you choose to, if you want to get it, it really has the whole incredible story.
cues.zh: 每一家卖油炸食品的夫妻小店，他们都在用普通食用油油炸。我想我没时间去细讲植物油加热后到底有多可怕。我并不是在推销自己的书，但我可以告诉你，在第9章的末尾，如果你愿意读读看，那里完整讲述了整件不可思议的真相。

cues.en: that I came across. These are just some of the toxic oxidation products that are in heated oils and the kinds of effects that they have. One of the aldehydes is a formal marker for your cancer risk. And aldehydes are created
cues.zh: 我无意中发现的。这些只是加热油中存在的几种有毒氧化产物，以及它们会造成的影响。其中一种醛类物质是癌症风险的明确指标。而这些醛类物质

cues.en: are just created in huge amounts when they fry food in polyunsaturated oils. And there was a woman who did an experiment where she just went to her local McDonald's and started just measuring the aldehydes in the fried chicken nuggets and the French fries. And she found hundreds of all kinds of oxidation products, but very high levels of these aldehydes.
cues.zh: 在用多不饱和油炸食物时，就会大量产生。曾有一位女士做过一个实验，她直接去了当地的 McDonald's，开始测量炸鸡块和薯条中的醛类含量。她发现了数百种各类氧化产物，而且这些醛类的含量极高。

cues.en: They are really terrifying. And the way I came across this whole story was that I actually, if you spend enough time talking to vegetable oil scientists, as I have done, one of them said, he said, you know what's going on in the restaurants, don't you? He says, ever since they've gone to these trans-free oils,
cues.zh: 它们真的很可怕。我之所以了解到这整个内幕，是因为如果你像我一样，花足够多的时间和植物油科学家交谈，其中一位就对我说，他说，你知道餐馆里现在是什么情况，对吧？他说，自从他们改用这些无反式脂肪的油之后，

cues.en: They have been having these horrible cleaning problems. They understand them as cleaning problems, because the fryers are getting clogged, because the oils turn into polymers. When they go through all this heated, that long molecule I showed you becomes degraded and broken up, and it changes into other kinds of polymers, like the polymers in paint, right?
cues.zh: 他们就遇到了非常可怕的清洁难题。他们以为这只是清洁问题，因为炸锅总是被堵住，油都变成了聚合物。经过反复高温加热，我之前展示给你们看的那种长分子就会降解、断裂，然后转化为其他种类的聚合物，就像油漆里的聚合物一样，明白吗？

cues.en: They would clog up the drains and they would have this gooey sticky stuff on the walls and they would try to scrape it off and nobody could scrape it off so they had to invent a new cleaner that was extra strong, that had extra strength chemicals in it that to use to try to depolymerize the stuff on the walls and in the drains and on the floors of all these fast food places. He said, the polymers, this,
cues.zh: 它们会堵塞下水道，墙上还会粘上一层黏糊糊的东西，怎么刮都刮不掉，所以他们不得不发明一种超强清洁剂，里面含有高强度化学物质，用来解聚所有这些快餐店墙壁上、下水道里和地板上的脏东西。他说，这些聚合物，这个……

cues.en: These degraded molecules were so unstable that when they would put the uniforms in the backs of trucks to go take them to the cleaners, the uniforms would spontaneously combust. And then when they took them to clean them and they put them in the dryers, there were still so many of these toxic chemicals in them that they would explode in the dryers. So I mean, just imagine we're just all putting this in our bodies.
cues.zh: 这些降解后的分子极不稳定，当他们把工作服扔进卡车后斗送去干洗时，衣服甚至会自燃。而送去清洗、放进烘干机后，里面残留的有毒化学物质依然多到会在烘干机里爆炸。我是说，想想看，我们居然把这种东西吃进肚子里。

cues.en: So, and that is why, you know, McDonald's used to fry their french fries in tallow, right? And I'm sure, and actually, and I've always thought, oh, they must taste a lot better, and in fact...
cues.zh: 所以，这就是为什么以前 McDonald's 会用牛油炸薯条，对吧？我一直觉得，噢，那味道肯定好得多，而事实上……

cues.en: Malcolm Gladwell who's a famous writer and now does a podcast and did this episode based really entirely on my book. One of the things he did was he went to McDonald's and he had them do some french fries in tallow and then had a taste test with everybody in the room and it was like hands down 100% tastier were the tallow french fries and I hope one day I can try some tallow french fries. I just want to say something about
cues.zh: 著名作家 Malcolm Gladwell，他现在也做播客，曾专门根据我的书做了一期节目。他做的一件事就是去了趟 McDonald's，让他们用牛油炸了些薯条，然后让现场所有人进行盲测，结果毫无悬念，100%的人都觉得牛油薯条更好吃，我希望有天我也能尝尝牛油炸的薯条。我只是想顺便提一下

cues.en: Olive oil, because everybody asked me about this, olive oil is a little different from a polyunsaturated seed oil because it only has one double bond, so it's a monounsaturated fat. So again, you think of a double bond as something that can open up and grab an oxygen, and that's oxidation, which causes inflammation. If you've only got one double bond, you've only got one hand out there, one other oxygen. So it's a bit more stable.
cues.zh: 橄榄油，因为大家总问我这个。橄榄油和多不饱和植物油有点不同，因为它只有一个双键，所以是单不饱和脂肪。再强调一下，你可以把双键看作是一个能张开抓住氧原子的结构，那就是氧化，会引发炎症。如果只有一个双键，就相当于只伸出一只手去抓另一个氧。所以它要相对稳定一些。

cues.en: And in the number of the experiments where they've done, where they've looked at what happens when you heat oils, the most toxic oxidation products are produced with polyunsaturated fats because they have the most bonds that can open up. There's a kind of olive oil that's kind of in it.
cues.zh: 在很多关于加热油脂反应的实验中，多不饱和脂肪产生的氧化毒性产物最多，因为它们含有最多容易断裂的化学键。而橄榄油大致处于这

cues.en: in between range. And the lowest oxidation products are, of course, with saturated fats, which have no double bonds. But monounsaturated fats are sort of in between there. And that's why I say, for salad dressings, use olive oil, right? Any non-heated application application.
cues.zh: 两种之间。当然，饱和脂肪产生的氧化产物最少，因为它们没有双键。不过单不饱和脂肪介于两者之间。所以这也是为什么我说，拌沙拉时可以用橄榄油，对吧？任何不需要加热的场景都行。

cues.en: Sound like a food executive. Anything you're doing to cook in the kitchen, use olive oil if you're not going to heat it. Don't use any polyunsaturated fats, and that includes canola oil, which is maybe a little bit of a better blend, but still it's...
cues.zh: 听起来像个食品行业高管似的。只要在厨房做饭不加热，就用橄榄油。别用任何多不饱和脂肪，包括菜籽油——菜籽油的配比可能稍好一点，但依然是……

cues.en: It's got polyunsaturates in there. And for cooking, really just use saturated fats. Try to say the word lard and not feel disgusted. And then buy some lard, which is fantastic to cook with. When I started cooking with lard, I couldn't get over how flaky, but we don't make pie crusts anymore, but really wonderful it is to cook with. And avoid fried food in restaurants, unless you really know that they're
cues.zh: 里面有多不饱和脂肪。至于做饭，真的就用饱和脂肪吧。试着念出“猪油”这个词，且别觉得恶心。然后去买点猪油，用来做饭简直绝了。当我刚开始用猪油做饭时，简直不敢相信它能做出多酥脆的口感——虽然我们现在不做派皮了——但用它做饭真的很棒。还要避免在餐馆吃油炸食品，除非你真能确定他们……

cues.en: unless you found the restaurant that cooks with tallow again. And this is, of course, entirely in contrast to everything that your experts are telling you, which is to replace saturated fats with polyunsaturated fatty acids.
cues.zh: 除非你找到了那家又重新用牛油做饭的餐馆。当然，这完全与专家们告诉你们的背道而驰，他们说要用多不饱和脂肪酸来替代饱和脂肪。

cues.en: And at this point, this recommendation now really is just hanging by a thread. And what they've done is they've really ignored all those randomized controlled clinical trials, which are the gold standard of evidence. And they're trying to, especially, again, coming out of Harvard, like endless studies based on their epidemiological data, a weaker, very weak kind of data to try to support this policy recommendation.
cues.zh: 而事到如今，这项建议其实已经是危如累卵了。他们所做的，完全就是无视了所有作为证据金标准的一系列随机对照临床试验。他们试图用——尤其是哈佛大学屡次抛出的——基于他们流行病学数据的无休止的研究，也就是一种更弱、极度薄弱的数据，来试图支撑这项政策建议。

cues.en: So that's it. These are just some pictures to show you, ancient foods. These are traditional fats. They're lovely. They taste good. And like Belinda and Gary, you can even fall in love forever eating lard. I bet you they're good singers too. Anyway, thank you.
cues.zh: 以上就是全部内容。给大家展示的这些图片，就是古老的食物。这些是传统油脂。它们非常棒。味道也很好。就像 Belinda 和 Gary 那样，吃猪油甚至能让你们相爱一生。我敢说他们唱歌肯定也很好听。总之，谢谢大家。
